newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian budget deficit narrowed in August.
newsitem.headline: Russian budget deficit narrowed in August.

text.p: Russia's budget deficit narrowed to 6.3 percent of gross domestic product in August, from 6.6 percent in July, using IMF methods of calculating both the deficit and GDP, finance ministry figures showed.

The IMF, which has backed Russian economic reforms with a $10 billion three-year loan, last month set a new 1996 target for the Russian budget deficit of 5.25 percent of gross domestic product. The previous target was four percent.
The fund delayed paying one tranche of the loan earlier this year because it was worried about low tax revenues and a wide budget deficit.
Jochen Wermuth, head of the ministry's economic expert group, said tax collection, especially VAT collection, had been rising in August.
He said new regulations that firms pay VAT and excise duties when they deliver goods should boost tax revenues further.
Firms previously paid tax only when they received payment for the goods they supplied. Frequent delays by purchasers also delayed tax payments.
